G9000.definition:
1.  fire-bearing  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of lightning, (Pindar):—; πυρφόροι ὀϊστοί arrows  with combustibles tied to them  , (Thucydides) 
2. in special senses, 
3.  epithet  of Zeus in reference to his lightnings, (Sophocles Tragicus); of Demeter, in reference to the torches used by her worshippers, (Euripides); of Artemis, (Sophocles Tragicus); but θεὸς πυρφόρος  the fire-bearing   god, the god  who produces plague   or  fever  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. ὁ πυρφόρος, in the Lacedaemonian army, was  the priest who kept the sacrificial fire  , which was never allowed to go out, (Xenophon Historicus); hence  proverbial  of a total defeat, ἔδεε δὲ μηδὲ πυρφόρον περιγενέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9002.definition: the beard  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; metaphorically , πώγων πυρός  a beard   or  tail   of fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9006.definition: to leave off work, to be remiss  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9007.definition:
1.  to sprinkle, besprinkle  , ῥάσσατε (i.e. δῶμα ὕδατι) (Odyssey by Homer); αἵματι βωμόν (Euripides):—;Pass., πύργοι αἵματι ἐρράδατ᾽ (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι δ᾽ ἐρράδαται τοῖχοι (Odyssey by Homer):—;of dust, ἵπποι ῥαίνοντο κονίηι (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  metaphorically , ῥ. τινὰ ὕμνωι (Pindar) 
3.  to sprinkle  , with  accusative  of the thing sprinkled, ῥαίνειν ἐς τὰ βλέφαρα  to sprinkle   (vinegar) in their eyes, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9012.definition:
1.  stitched, patched  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  metaphorically   strung together, continuous  , of verses, (Pindar) 
3.  worked with the needle  : ῥαπτόν, οῦ,  an embroidered carpet  , (Xenophon Historicus); ῥαπτὴ σφαῖρα  a stitched   ball, of divers colours, [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
 (ML)

G9013.definition:
1.  to sew   or  stitch together, stich  , (Iliad by Homer):—; Mid., ῥάπτεσθαι ὀχετὸν δερμάτων  to make oneself   a pipe of leather, (Herdotus Historicus); ῥαψάμενος τουτί (i.e. τὸ προσκεφάλαιον)  having got   it  stitched  , (Aristophanes Comicus); but also,  to sew on   or  to one  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., ἐρράφθαι τὸ χεῖλος  to have   one's lip  sewed up  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2.  metaphorically   to devise, contrive, plot  , (Homer), etc.;  proverbial , τὸ ὑπόδημα ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης you  made the shoe  , but Aristagoras put it on, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9018.definition:
1.  the lower part of the back, the chine  , (Iliad by Homer): then,  the spine   or  backbone  , ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγῆναι to be impaled, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9022.definition:
1.  a saying, speaking, speech  , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ Σκυθῶν ῥῆσις the Scythian  phrase  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  a resolution, declaration  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  a tale, legend  , (Pindar) 
4.  a phrase   or  passage, a speech in a play  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9024.definition:
1.  stated, specified  , (Iliad by Homer); ἐς χρόνον ῥητόν at a  set   or  stated   time, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμέραι ῥ. (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς γέρασι with  fixed   prerogatives, (Thucydides); ῥ. ἀργύριον a  stated   sum, (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς  on stated terms, on certain conditions  , (Herdotus Historicus):—; adverb  ῥητῶς,  expressly, distinctly  , (New Testament) 
2.  spoken of, known, famous  , (Hesiod) 
3.  that may be spoken   or  told  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ῥητὸν ἄρρητόν τ᾽ ἔπος, Lat.  fas nefasque , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. in Mathem., ῥητά are  rational quantities  , opposite to surds  ἄλογα); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9025.definition:
frost, cold  , Lat.  frigus , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
 (ML)

G9026.definition: a root  :  metaphorically   a stem, race   (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9029.definition:
1. ionic and epic ῥοιή,  a pomegranate-tree  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. the fruit,  a pomegranate  , (Homeric Hymns) 
3.  a knob shaped like a pomegranate  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9030.definition: to whistle  , Lat.  stridere , (Iliad by Homer); of a snake,  to hiss  , (Hesiod):—;Pass.  to rush through   the  air  , ἐρροίζητο (3rd  singular   pluperfect ) [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G9031.definition:
1.  the whistling   or  whizzing   of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer):—;any  whistling   or  piping sound  , as of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  rushing motion, a rush, swing  , (Plutarch) 
Formed from the sound. (ML)

G9033.definition:
1.  a club, cudgel  , thicker at the buttend; used to cudgel an ass, (Iliad by Homer); to walk with, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;  a war-club   or  mace  , shod with metal, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. = ῥόπτρον III, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9034.definition:
ῥοπή , -ῆς, ἡ 
 (ῥέπω, to incline) [in LXX:  Isa.40:15  (שַׁחַק), etc. ;] 
 inclination downwards, as the turn of the scale : L, mg., for ῥιπή, which see,  1Co.15:52  (see Tdf., in l).†
 (AS)

G9036.definition: a rushing stream, a torrent  , (Thucydides); ὁ ῥ. τοῦ πυρός, of  a stream of lava  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9037.definition: to bring into measure   or  proportion  : generally,  to order, to educate, train  , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—; metaphorically , ῥ. λύπην ὅπου  to define   the place of grief, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid., ῥ. πλόκαμον  to arrange one's   hair, (Euripides):—;Pass., νηλεῶς ὧδ᾽ ἐρρύθμισμαι thus ruthlessly  am I brought to order  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9038.definition:
1.  measured motion, time, rhythm  , Lat.  numerus , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: —; ἐν ῥυθμῷ in  time  ,  Virgil  's  in numerum  , (Xenophon Historicus); μετὰ ῥυθμοῦ (Thucydides); θάττονα ῥυθμὸν ἐπάγειν to play in quicker  time  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  proportion   or symmetry of parts, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. generally,  arrangement, order  , (Euripides) 
4.  the state   or  condition of the soul, temper, disposition  , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 
5.  the form   or  shape   of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); of a breastplate, (Xenophon Historicus) 
6.  the wise, manner   or  fashion   of a thing, (Euripides); τίς ῥ. φόνο; what  kind   of slaughter? (Euripides) (ML)

G9043.definition: to keep the Sabbath  , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G9046.definition:
1. mostly in  plural   covering: the covering of a shield  , (Euripides):  a large cloak  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  a pack-saddle  , (Strabo Geographus) 
3.  a pile  , ὅπλων (Plutarch) (ML)

G9050.definition:
1.  rotten, decayed, unsound, cracked  , (Plato Philosophus)—; adverb , σαθρῶς ἱδρυμένος built on  unsound   foundations, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  metaphorically , πρίν τι καὶ σαθρὸν ἐγγίνεσθαί σφι before any  unsound thought   comes into their heads, i. e. before they prove traitors, (Herdotus Historicus); ς. λόγοι (Euripides) 
 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9052.definition:
1.  a triangular musical instrument with four strings  , Lat.  sambuca , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  an engine of like form   used in sieges, (Plutarch) (ML)

G9058.definition: a satrapy, the office   or  province of a satrap  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9059.definition:
a satrap, viceroy  , Lat.  satrapa , (Xenophon Historicus) 
 
Persian word. (ML)

G9063.definition:
1.  a Siren  : in  plural  Σειρῆνες, αἱ,  the Sirens  , mythical sisters on the south coast of Italy, who enticed seamen by their songs, and then slew them, (Odyssey by Homer) (Homer) only knows of  two  , whence epic dual.  genitive  Σειρήνοιιν. 
2.  metaphorically   a Siren, deceitful woman  , (Euripides):  the Siren charm   of eloquence, (Aeschines Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9065.definition: a plank  :  metaphorically   a leaf of papyrus: —;   generally,  the page of a book  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G9069.definition:
a standard  , (Polybius Historicus):—;  a band under one standard  , the Roman  manipulus  , (Polybius Historicus) 
 (ML)

G9073.definition:
1.  strength, might  , (Iliad by Homer):—;with  infinitive , σθ. πολεμίζειν  strength   to war, (Iliad by Homer); σθ. ὥστε καθελεῖν (Euripides); σθένει  by force  , (Sophocles Tragicus); λόγῳ τε καὶ σθένει both by right and  might  , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ὑπὸ σθένους (Euripides); παντὶ σθένει with all  one's might  , (Thucydides) 
2.  strength, might  , of all kinds moral as well as physical, σθένος τῆς ἀληθείας (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀγγέλων σθ. their  might   or  authority  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3.  a force   of men, like δύναμις, (Iliad by Homer) 
4.  metaphorically , like Lat. vis for  copia, a quantity, profusion  , (Pindar) 
5.  periphrastic , like βίη, ἴς, μένος, as σθένος Ἰδομενῆος, Ὠρίωνος, for Idomeneus, Orion, themselves, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9075.definition:
1.  silently  , σῖγα ἔχειν to be  silent  , (Sophocles Tragicus); κάθησο σῖγα (Aristophanes Comicus); alone, σῖγα  hush! be still!   (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;the public crier proclaiming  silence   said σῖγα πᾶς (i.e. ἔστω); (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  under one's breath, in a whisper, secretly  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9076.definition: an implement   or  tool of iron  , σιδηρίων ἐπαί̈ειν to feel  iron  , not to be proof against it, (Herdotus Historicus); θερμὰ σιδήρια hot  irons  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9086.definition: want of corn   or  food  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9089.definition:
1. ς. ἀνάγκη the task  of grinding and baking  , (Euripides) 
2. as  Substantive   one that ground the corn in the handmill  , (Thucydides); mostly  feminine   a baking-woman  , (Herdotus Historicus); γυναῖκες ς. (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9090.definition:
1.  silence  , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; σιωπὴν ποιεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); ἦν ς. there was  a hush   or  calm  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2.  the habit of silence  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3.  dative  σιωπῇ as  adverb ,  in silence  , (Homer), attic 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9096.definition:
a carpenter's axe   or  adze  , used for smoothing the trunks of trees, different from the πέλεκυς, (Odyssey by Homer) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9098.definition: a covering, shelter, protection  , (Xenophon Historicus):—;with  genitive , ἐν σκέπῃ τοῦ πολέμου  under shelter from   war, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπὸ τὴν Ῥωμαίων σκέπην under their  protection  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)
